title: Assessing Estimated Expenditure of Providing Cash Component of Baby Bonus to Single Unwed Parents
what_it_is: Assessing Estimated Expenditure of Providing Cash Component of Baby Bonus to Single Unwed Parents

sections.label: Baby Bonus for single unwed parents
sections.summary: A Member asked whether the Ministry will consider studying the estimated costs of the Baby Bonus cash component for single unwed parents.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Social and Family Development whether the Ministry will consider studying the estimated costs of providing the cash component of the Baby Bonus to single unwed parents.

sections.label: HDB housing requests and societal norms
sections.summary: HDB assesses housing requests holistically based on individual circumstances, and policies reflect prevailing societal norms and values of parenthood within marriage.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: HDB also assesses their requests for housing holistically, based on their individual circumstances.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: It is not an issue of cost, let alone whether we will study it, but that each of these policies reflect prevailing societal norms and values, that of parenthood within marriage.

sections.label: Salaries of single unwed parents
sections.summary: Data shows single unwed parents under age 35 have a median salary of $700.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Our own data shows that single unwed parents under age 35 have a median salary of $700.

sections.label: Reliefs and stigma for single parents
sections.summary: A Member hoped MSF would view the Working Mother's Child Relief and Parenthood Tax Rebate from stigma and discrimination rather than fiscal cost.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Two, for the Working Mother's Child Relief and the Parenthood Tax Rebate, I hope MSF can look at this not from a fiscal cost standpoint, but one of stigma and discrimination.

sections.label: Policies cannot be reduced or recycled
sections.summary: The speaker said Members feel the same and that policies cannot be reduced, reused or recycled even when not used for their intended purpose.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: I think Members in this House feel the same.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: And even when they are not used up for its intended purpose, policies cannot be reduced, reused or recycled.

sections.label: Changing rationale of Working Mother's Child Relief
sections.summary: A Member agreed policies serve a purpose but can change, citing the Budget's change to the rationale of the Working Mother's Child Relief.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
sentences.text: I do agree with Minister – the policies are there for a purpose.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
sentences.text: But policies can change and that is why in this Budget, we changed the whole rationale of the Working Mother's Child Relief.

sections.label: Support versus incentive distinction
sections.summary: A distinction must be made between support and incentive, and if that shifts in future, they will move with it.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: Because we must make a distinction between support and incentive.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: If that shifts in future, certainly, we will move with it.
